Experience:

  • Previous experience in home health, hospice, home care or a related clinical/administrative setting is preferred.

Knowledge:

Understanding of home health/home care regulations and insurance verification processes.

Communication:

Excellent verbal and written skills; ability to listen actively and communicate with empathy.

Organization:

  • Strong attention to detail, ability to multitask, and manage a high volume of information.
  • Technical Skills: Proficiency with computer systems and databases.

The Goal

The Intake Coordinator bridges the gap between referral sources and home care services, ensuring the right patient receives the right care at the right time while maintaining regulatory adherence and strong customer relationships.

job.title: Regional Director of Operations – Skilled Nursing Facilities
job.description:
Location: Granite City, IL and surrounding region (northward)

Position Summary
The Regional Director of Operations (RDO) provides strategic and operational leadership for approximately seven skilled nursing facilities located in Granite City, IL and the surrounding region to the north. This leader ensures each community delivers exceptional clinical care, operational performance, regulatory compliance, financial stability, and a culture that supports residents, families, and staff. The RDO serves as a key partner to Administrators, Regional Clinical leadership, and the corporate executive team.

Key Responsibilities

Operational Leadership
Provide direct oversight of daily operations for assigned skilled nursing facilities, ensuring strong performance across census, quality, compliance, staffing, and financial metrics.

Coach and support Facility Administrators to achieve organizational goals and maintain consistent operational excellence.

Ensure effective implementation of company policies, systems, and best practices.

Regulatory & Quality Compliance
Lead preparedness and response for state and federal surveys, ensuring ongoing compliance with CMS, IDPH, and other regulatory bodies.

Partner with clinical and compliance teams to improve quality outcomes, reduce deficiencies, and maintain strong survey histories.

Monitor QAPI programs and drive continuous improvement initiatives.

Financial & Business Performance
Manage regional budgets, financial forecasts, and performance indicators across all assigned facilities.

Analyze financial and operational data to identify opportunities for growth, efficiencies, and expense management.

Support optimization of reimbursement, payer mix, admissions processes, and overall revenue cycle performance.

People Leadership & Culture
Recruit, mentor, and develop Facility Administrators and leadership teams to ensure stability and strong performance.

Promote a culture of accountability, teamwork, high standards of care, and employee engagement.

Partner with HR to address staffing needs, retention strategies, and leadership development.

Strategic & Relationship Management
Build strong relationships with community partners, referral sources, residents, families, and regulatory agencies.

Collaborate with corporate leadership to develop and execute strategic initiatives at the regional level.

Represent the organization professionally and foster a positive reputation within the healthcare community.


Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred (Healthcare Administration, Business, or related field).

Minimum 3–5 years of multi-facility leadership experience in skilled nursing/long-term care—overseeing multiple SNFs is required.

Active Illinois Nursing Home Administrator (NHA) license strongly preferred.

Demonstrated success in managing operational, financial, and regulatory outcomes across multiple facilities.

Strong knowledge of CMS regulations, IDPH requirements, and value-based care metrics.

Proven ability to coach and motivate teams, build culture, and lead through change.

Excellent communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.

Ability to travel regularly within the assigned region.


What We Offer
Competitive salary and performance-based bonus structure

Comprehensive benefits package

Opportunities for professional development and career growth

Supportive leadership and collaborative multi-site team environment

Equal Opportunity Employer

We are seeking a dedicated and experienced Nursing Home Administrator to oversee the efficient and compassionate operation of our nursing home facility. The ideal candidate will be responsible for managing day-to-day operations, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements, and creating a supportive and caring environment for residents and staff. The Nursing Home Administrator will play a crucial role in maintaining high-quality care standards, fostering a positive culture, and implementing strategic initiatives to enhance the overall well-being of residents.

Responsibilities:

Operational Leadership

  • Oversee the daily operations of the nursing home, ensuring the delivery of high-quality care services.
  • Collaborate with department heads to streamline processes and improve overall efficiency.
  • Implement policies and procedures to maintain compliance with local, state, and federal regulations.

Staff Management

  • Recruit, train, and supervise nursing home staff, including nurses, administrative personnel, and support staff.
  • Foster a positive and inclusive work environment, promoting teamwork and professional development.
  • Conduct regular performance evaluations and address any issues or concerns promptly.

Resident Care

  • Ensure the provision of compassionate and person-centered care to residents.
  • Work closely with healthcare professionals to develop and implement care plans tailored to individual resident needs.
  • Address resident and family concerns promptly and effectively.

Budget and Financial Management

  • Develop and manage the nursing home budget, ensuring financial sustainability.
  • Monitor expenses, identify cost-saving opportunities, and optimize resource allocation.

Quality Assurance

  • Implement quality assurance programs to assess and improve the overall quality of care and services.
  • Conduct regular audits and inspections to ensure compliance with established standards.

Community Engagement

  • Build positive relationships with residents, families, and the local community.
  • Actively participate in community events and outreach initiatives to enhance the nursing home's reputation.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, or a related field preferred
  • Current state licensure as a Nursing Home Administrator.
  • Proven experience in a leadership role within a nursing home or long-term care facility.
  • Strong knowledge of healthcare regulations and compliance requirements.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to make sound decisions in a fast-paced and challenging environment.

If you are a dynamic leader with a passion for enhancing the lives of elderly residents and creating a positive workplace culture, we invite you to apply for this rewarding opportunity as a Nursing Home Administrator.

Benefits
Medical, Dental, Vision, etc.

Equal Opportunity Employer

job.title: Asset Manager
job.description:
Role:

• Responsible for maximizing the value and performance of a diverse real estate portfolio.
• Provide proactive financial oversight, operational optimization, and strategic execution from acquisition through disposition.
• Partner closely with Leasing, Finance and Operations to drive Net Operating Income growth and ensure each asset reaches its full potential.
• Execute Business Plans: Develop and own asset-level strategies to maximize NOI, cash flow, and overall valuation
• Performance Analysis: Rigorously analyze property performance against budgets, forecasts and original underwriting assumptions
• Market Intelligence: Monitor regional trends, rent comparable, and competitive positions to ensure Omninet remains a market leader
• Budgeting & Forecasting: Be a key leader in the preparation of annual operating budgets, capital plans, and long-range financial projections
• Compliance: Support debt compliance, lender reporting and covenant tracking to maintain optimal capital structure
• P&L Oversight: Review monthly financial statement; identify variances to senior management and implement corrective actions when necessary
• Capital Projects: Oversee value-add initiatives, including renovations and repositioning
• Evaluate ROI on capital spend and ensure projects stay on time and under budget
• Risk Mitigation: Monitor property taxes, insurance, and regulatory compliance to protect the portfolio from exposure
• Stakeholder Communication: Prepare high-level asset reporting for internal leadership and contribute to quarterly portfolio reviews
• Transaction Support: Assist in the due diligence and onboarding of new acquisitions and provide critical data for asset dispositions
• 4+ years of experience in asset management, real estate finance, or property operations
• Strong understanding of property-level P&Ls, NOI drivers, and real estate fundamentals
• Operates with a proactive, results-oriented “owner mindset”
• Advanced Excel skills for financial modeling and budgeting; familiarity with Yardi is preferred.
• Able to pivot from granular financial discussions with accounting to high-level strategy meetings with the CEO and Managing Directors.
• MBA, MSRE, or professional certifications (ARGUS, CPM, CFA a plus)
• Comp $100-125K

Equal Opportunity Employer

job.title: Director Patient Care
job.description:
We are looking for a full-time Director of Patient Care Services (DPCS) for our hospice program, servicing the Greater Los Angeles areas and adjoining communities. The DPCS is a full-time executive leadership position with overall clinical management responsibility of the hospice program. The DPCS is responsible for the overall successful delivery of care to patients and families and serves as the liaison between the Administrator, clinical staff, patients, families and members of the community.

The DPCS supervises the clinical staff, including team mangers, contracted services, On-Call and continuous care staff and assists in the hiring and retention of staff. The DPCS contributes to and implements a Qualify Assurance program, participates in staff training, assures qualified clinical staff is hired and assures only eligible patients are admitted to the program and receive hospice care. DPCS assumes lead responsibility for patient advocacy and carries out the organizations mission, goals, objectives and policies.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Graduate of an accredited school of nursing with Bachelor degree or higher in nursing.
  • Current California RN license. Certification in Hospice and Palliative Nursing preferred.
  • Five years work experience, with at least three years in a hospice or home health.
  • Demonstrate high level of competency in performance of professional nursing functions.
  • Ability to plan, organize, delegate and manage effectively and efficiently.
  • Ability to make effective decisions under time pressure.
  • Ability to supervise and evaluate staff.
  • Knowledge of regulatory aspects of hospice.
  • Excellent communication (verbal and written) and personable skills.
  • Ability to interact professionally and effectively with staff, members of the public,
  • patients and families, as well as ability to direct others.
  • Valid driver's license, auto insurance, reliable/well maintained transportation.
  • Able to utilize computers and be comfortable with electronic medical and other records.

Benefits: 

  • Earn a competitive salary based on experience $125k-$140k
  • Work life balance with holiday pay, sick pay and vacation pay.
  • Health insurance including dental and vision.
  • Tuition reimbursement assistance
  • 401k and life insurance plans
  • Great team with professionals who value and respect one another.
  • Gain recognition while serving patients and families when they are at their most vulnerable.
  • Work for an organization that has been recognized as one of the best places to work.

job.title: Infection Preventionist Nurse Opportunity!
job.description:
We are seeking an experienced Infection Preventionist Nurse to join our skilled nursing team in the Uptown/Edgewater area of Chicago. This is an important leadership role responsible for developing, implementing, monitoring, and continuously improving the facility’s infection prevention and control program.

The ideal candidate is a knowledgeable and proactive Nurse who understands skilled nursing facility regulations, infection prevention practices, antibiotic stewardship, surveillance, and CMS requirements and can effectively partner with nursing leadership and the interdisciplinary team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Direct and oversee the facility’s Infection Prevention and Control Program.
  • Conduct ongoing infection surveillance, identify trends, and implement appropriate interventions.
  • Investigate infections and potential outbreaks and coordinate appropriate response measures.
  • Develop, implement, and monitor infection prevention policies, procedures, and protocols.
  • Ensure compliance with CMS, CDC, IDPH, OSHA, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Monitor staff compliance with hand hygiene, PPE, isolation precautions, and other infection prevention practices.
  • Provide education and competency training to nursing and other facility staff.
  • Participate in Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) initiatives.
  • Maintain accurate infection prevention documentation, surveillance records, and reports.
  • Work closely with the Director of Nursing, Medical Director, Administrator, and interdisciplinary team.
  • Monitor antibiotic utilization and support the facility’s antibiotic stewardship program.
  • Prepare for and participate in regulatory surveys and infection prevention audits.
  • Identify opportunities for improvement and develop corrective action plans when necessary.

Qualifications

  • Current Illinois Nursing license required.
  • Previous experience in long-term care/skilled nursing strongly preferred.
  • Infection Prevention and Control experience preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of CDC and CMS infection prevention guidelines and long-term care regulations.
  • Experience with infection surveillance, outbreak investigation, and employee education.
  • Strong clinical assessment, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently while effectively collaborating with nursing and facility leadership.
  • Infection Preventionist certification (CIC, IP-BC, or similar) is a plus.

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Infection Preventionist Nurse who wants to take ownership of a critical clinical program and have a direct impact on resident safety, quality outcomes, regulatory compliance, and staff education.

job.title: Nursing Home Administrator
job.description:
We are seeking a dynamic and experienced **Nursing Home Administrator (LNHA)** to lead the daily operations of our skilled nursing facility. This is an outstanding opportunity for a passionate leader who is committed to providing exceptional resident care, fostering employee engagement, maintaining regulatory compliance, and driving operational excellence. The ideal candidate is a hands-on leader with a proven track record of building strong teams, improving quality outcomes, and achieving financial and census goals.

Responsibilities

  • Oversee the overall operations of the skilled nursing facility, ensuring the highest standards of resident care and customer service.
  • Ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local regulations, including CMS and Department of Health requirements.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop department managers while promoting a positive, team-oriented culture.
  • Monitor and improve quality measures, survey readiness, infection prevention initiatives, and resident satisfaction.
  • Partner with the Director of Nursing and interdisciplinary team to ensure exceptional clinical outcomes and regulatory compliance.
  • Develop and manage the facility's operating budget while maintaining financial performance and controlling expenses.
  • Drive census growth by collaborating with admissions, marketing, hospitals, physicians, and community partners.
  • Oversee risk management, life safety compliance, and emergency preparedness.
  • Review operational metrics and implement performance improvement initiatives to achieve company goals.
  • Foster strong relationships with residents, families, physicians, referral sources, and community organizations.
  • Ensure appropriate staffing levels and support employee recruitment, retention, engagement, and professional development.
  • Lead Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) initiatives and implement action plans as needed.
  • Promote a culture centered on compassion, accountability, respect, and excellence.

Qualifications

  • Current Nursing Home Administrator (LNHA) license in the state of Ohio.
  • Bachelor's degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Public Health, or a related field (Master's degree preferred).
  • Minimum of 2-5 years of Nursing Home Administrator experience in a skilled nursing or long-term care setting.
  • Demonstrated success with regulatory compliance, survey management, census growth, quality improvement, and financial performance.
  • Strong knowledge of CMS regulations, reimbursement, Medicare, Medicaid, and long-term care operations.
  • Exceptional leadership, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to motivate teams, manage multiple priorities, and thrive in a fast-paced healthcare environment.

Why Join Us?

We believe our employees are our greatest asset. We offer a collaborative work environment where leaders are empowered to make a meaningful impact on the lives of residents and staff every day. In addition to a competitive compensation package, we provide opportunities for professional growth, leadership development, and the support needed to build a successful and rewarding career in long-term care.

If you are a compassionate leader with a passion for excellence and a commitment to serving seniors, we encourage you to apply today.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer considering all qualified applicants in accordance with federal, state, and local laws. We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in a manner consistent with applicable laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles City Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We partially sponsor health insurance as required by the Affordable Care Act; provide Sick Pay as required by state or local law; and offer a daily transportation subsidy in certain situations.

job.title: Physical Therapist Assistant
job.description:
The Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) plays a critical role in supporting licensed physical therapists in delivering high-quality rehabilitative care to patients recovering from injury, surgery, or managing chronic conditions.

This position involves implementing treatment plans designed by physical therapists, monitoring patient progress, and adjusting therapeutic activities as needed to optimize recovery outcomes.

The PTA works closely with patients to provide hands-on therapy, educate them on exercises and mobility techniques, and ensure safety throughout the rehabilitation process.

Collaboration with interdisciplinary healthcare teams is essential to coordinate care and communicate patient status effectively.

Ultimately, the PTA contributes significantly to improving patients' physical function, reducing pain, and enhancing their overall quality of life through compassionate and skilled therapeutic interventions.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Completion of an accredited Physical Therapist Assistant program.
  • Current and valid state licensure or certification as a Physical Therapist Assistant.
  • Basic life support (BLS) certification.
  • Strong understanding of human anatomy, physiology, and therapeutic exercise principles.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively interact with patients and healthcare team members.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working in outpatient, inpatient, or rehabilitation settings.
  • Familiarity with electronic medical records (EMR) systems.
  • Additional certifications such as CPR or specialty therapy techniques.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with diverse patient populations including pediatric and geriatric patients.
  • Continuing education in advanced therapeutic modalities or patient care techniques.

Responsibilities (may include but not limited to):

  • Assist physical therapists in executing individualized treatment plans for patients with various musculoskeletal and neurological conditions.
  • Provide therapeutic exercises and manual therapy under the supervision of a physical therapist.
  • Monitor and document patient responses to treatment, reporting progress and any concerns to the supervising therapist.
  • Educate patients and their families on home exercise programs, proper use of assistive devices, and injury prevention strategies.
  • Maintain a safe and clean treatment environment, ensuring all equipment is properly sanitized and functional.
  • Collaborate with healthcare professionals to coordinate patient care and participate in team meetings as required.
  • Adhere to all regulatory, ethical, and organizational standards related to patient confidentiality and care.

Skills:

The required skills enable the Physical Therapist Assistant to competently deliver therapeutic interventions and ensure patient safety during treatment sessions.

Strong communication skills are essential for educating patients and collaborating with physical therapists and other healthcare professionals.

Knowledge of anatomy and physiology guides the PTA in applying appropriate exercises and modalities tailored to each patient's condition.

Preferred skills such as experience with electronic medical records streamline documentation and enhance care coordination.

Additionally, advanced certifications and familiarity with diverse patient populations allow the PTA to provide more specialized and effective care, contributing to improved patient outcomes.
